llm.note: Gemini free tier. Version 2: the AI reading decides (incident or not, type, case facts, date). A second reader (a different model) checks every report where the first reader and the rules disagree; the expert settles only three-way splits. Judges decide whether two close reports are the same incident. The expert re-checks the riskiest "same" verdicts (audit). The "-latest" names always point to a current model, so a retired model never stops the layer. rpd/rpm are the free limits shown in AI Studio (Nov 2026). Each model has its own daily allowance and the three lite readers together give only ~610 a day, so 27 Nov 2026 four more models this key can use were added as readers (probed on engine-test): the engine read nothing for 17 hours a day once those 610 were gone.
llm.valid_note: version: the form; bump it to re-read every report (newest first, capped by per_run.reread). valid_from: the oldest form whose second and expert readings still decide. Raise it only when the meaning of the answers changes, never for an added question: discarding them made 386 reports unsettled at once (25 Nov 2026).

organised.note: Groups as publicly reported. Leaders are named as the press names them: accused, not convicted unless a report says so. Never stored: names of juveniles or of victims of sexual offences. Community labels (e.g. 'Irani gang') are not used as group names.

groups.name: Koyta gangs
groups.about: Media and police label for youth crews who terrorise streets with sickles (koyta): vandalising vehicles, threatening shopkeepers, attacking rivals. Mostly loose crews, often with minors, rather than one organisation.

situations.note: Public order: protests, bandhs, road blockades, strikes, unrest, prohibitory orders; also emergencies (bomb threats, evacuations, collapses, gas leaks, floods) and disruptions of transport and services (metro or bus breakdowns, road closures, diversions, traffic jams, water or power cuts). Most serious kind first. The word patterns only find candidates: the AI reading decides.
